questions.q: What kind of thing is an Azure Quantum workspace?
options: A separate quantum-only cloud account outside normal Azure billing and governance
An ordinary Azure resource provisioned inside a resource group/subscription, billed and governed like any other Azure resource
A physical quantum computer dedicated to one customer
A local application installed on the developer's own machine
questions.explain: A workspace is provisioned like any other Azure resource (storage account, VM) inside a resource group and subscription, using the same billing, RBAC, and tagging the rest of Azure uses.

questions.q: Besides a resource group, what does creating an Azure Quantum workspace specifically require?
options: A linked storage account to hold job inputs/outputs, and at least one provider added
A pre-existing quantum circuit uploaded in advance
A dedicated physical QPU reserved exclusively for that workspace
Nothing beyond choosing a workspace name
questions.explain: A workspace needs a linked Azure Storage account (for job data) and explicitly selected providers -- providers aren't automatically available just because the workspace exists.

questions.q: Why does adding a provider matter per-workspace rather than being automatic?
options: Each workspace explicitly lists which simulators/estimator/hardware providers it has access to, and some providers require separate access approval or terms
Providers are a purely cosmetic label with no functional effect
All Azure Quantum workspaces automatically get every provider with no configuration
Providers can only ever be set once and never changed afterward
questions.explain: Providers are explicitly attached to a workspace (at creation or later), and some hardware providers require separate access/terms beyond just creating the workspace.

questions.q: In the `az quantum workspace create` command, what does `--provider-sku-list` control?
options: The Azure region the workspace is deployed to
Which providers and plan tiers the workspace is granted access to
The name of the linked storage account only
The programming language used for job submission
questions.explain: The provider-sku-list argument declares which providers (simulator, estimator, hardware partners) and tiers this workspace should be able to submit jobs to.

questions.q: How does a Python script using the `azure-quantum` package's `Workspace` object typically authenticate to Azure, according to the lesson?
options: It requires a separate dedicated Azure Quantum API key unrelated to normal Azure auth
Through existing Azure credentials, such as an az login session or a managed identity -- no separate Azure Quantum-specific key
It cannot authenticate from Python at all, only from the Portal
By embedding the subscription owner's password directly in the script
questions.explain: Workspace connections reuse standard Azure credential flows (az login session or managed identity) rather than a separate Azure Quantum API key system.
